title: Comparison of vertical breast displacement between two different sports bra designs
publisher: International Society of Biomechanics in Sports (ISBS) Conference Proceedings
claims: Thirty female collegiate athletes (mean age 22.33 ± 2.7 years, mean body mass 57.3 ± 5.9 kg, BMI 20.9 ± 1.4) with bra sizes B75 to C70 walked at 3 km/h, jogged at 6 km/h and ran at 9 km/h on a treadmill under no bra, encapsulation bra and compression bra conditions.

During running, vertical breast displacement was 42.6 ± 13.3 mm on the right and 48.8 ± 12.1 mm on the left with no bra, 23.3 ± 8.8 mm and 22.8 ± 7.4 mm with an encapsulation bra, and 18.9 ± 5.7 mm and 19.1 ± 6.4 mm with a compression bra.
Sports bras reduced vertical breast displacement by more than 50% during jogging compared with no bra.
The compression bra produced significantly less vertical breast displacement than the encapsulation bra during jogging and running (p < 0.05).
The encapsulation bra allowed more independent breast motion, while the compression bra produced almost symmetrical displacement between left and right sides.
Vertical displacement during walking and jogging did not differ significantly between the two sports bra types.
